title: Audit courier: customer-managed storage adapters, resumable uploads, and VPC/on-prem forwarding
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: Private and VPC customers require robust audit-log forwarding that can write directly to customer-managed storage (S3/GCS/Azure Blob or on-prem object stores) while meeting compliance guarantees (durability, immutability where requested, retention metadata) and operating reliably across air-gapped or intermittent networks. Existing audit shipper prototypes assume always-on egress and single-request uploads which fail in constrained on-prem environments and do not satisfy customers who mandate customer-side encryption keys (CMEK) and strict bucket policies.

Goal: Design and implement an "audit courier" subsystem for Private/VPC/on-prem deployments that: (1) supports customer-managed storage adapters with pluggable auth models (pre-signed URLs, STS role-assume, SAS tokens, HSM-backed credentials), (2) provides resumable/multipart upload semantics with local durable spool and backpressure controls, (3) validates and enforces customer bucket policies and retention rules before egress, (4) supports envelope encryption and optional server-side or client-side encryption using customer keys, (5) integrates with RBAC v2 and SSO admin flows for operator binding and key rotation, and (6) ships strong observability and runbook guidance for failures and audits.

Scope: This ticket covers design, prototype implementation for S3-compatible targets + GCS, bucket policy validator, multipart upload manager, local disk spool with backpressure and retention-correct metadata manifests, admin console binding UI hooks for private customers, and a test matrix for intermittent network and large file (>5GB) uploads. Productionization (scaling, HA, formal compliance certs) will be a follow-up.

Design notes and decisions: 
- Local spool: use a write-ahead directory per-tenant with per-file manifest (json lines) containing: source-offsets, per-object checksum (SHA256), retention-policy-id, encryption-envelope headers. Spool files are written atomically via temp->rename and periodically compacted. This avoids losing events during transient egress outages.
- Resumable uploads: implement multipart/resume across S3/GCS. For S3 we will prefer the multipart upload API; for GCS we will use their resumable upload sessions. For on-prem object stores that only support PUT, implement chunked stage+compose where possible. Upload coordinator tracks per-part etags and can resume from last committed part.
- Auth adapters: abstract an adapter interface for auth: presigned_url, sts_assume_role, oauth_service_account, sas_token. For customer-managed KMS flows (CMEK), support two patterns: (A) Redwood-managed envelope keys encrypted with customer KMS (we keep only envelope ciphertext), or (B) customer-managed presigned URLs where encryption is on the storage side (server-side encryption with customer key). Choice depends on airgap constraints and compliance requests.
- Bucket policy validator: a pre-flight check that validates ACLs, object-lock, and if present, immutability settings. Validator runs at bind time (operator console) and again during periodic audits. If bucket policy prevents required metadata writes (e.g., denies PutObject with x-amz-meta-*), the validator rejects and surfaces remediation steps.
- Retention & manifests: every upload includes a signed manifest object placed alongside logs that contains retention metadata (retention start, TTL, legal hold flag). For S3 object lock support we will surface an API for operators to request the component set object-lock flags during upload.
- Backpressure and flow control: expose two operational modes: write-through (synchronous: return success once upload to customer storage completes) and buffered (ack to local ingesters immediately and background-deliver). Buffered mode has configurable local disk quota per-tenant and policy for throttling ingestion (reject vs shed oldest).
- Integrity verification: after upload, coordinator validates checksums and writes an upload receipt into a privileged path in the customer's bucket (or an agreed manifest location). Receipts are signed by the service's signing key to allow offline verification by customers.
- Airgap options: for fully air-gapped installs, support operator-driven manual handoff: produce encrypted tarballs with manifests to an operator-specified USB or internal transfer point; provide tooling to resume ingestion on an external staging host that has egress to customer storage.

Security considerations: 
- Secrets: credentials for auth adapters are stored in the private deployment's KMS/HSM and never leave the operator-controlled plane. Where possible, use short-lived credentials (STS) and rotate aggressively.
- RBAC integration: binding/unbinding of customer buckets is gated by RBAC v2 roles (audit-admin or infra-operator). Console flows for adding a sink require SSO sign-in and an approval step for sensitive customers.
- Audit trail: every forwarder operation emits structured audit events (bind, unbind, upload-start, upload-part, upload-complete, verification-failed) with tenant scoping. These events are retained separately from customer logs and are subject to stricter retention.
- Failure modes: an attacker who can access local spool files could exfiltrate logs; mitigate with envelope encryption and disk-level encryption. For on-prem, provide a hardening guide recommending encrypted filesystems and access controls.

Operational requirements and metrics: 
- Metrics: spool_queue_size_bytes, active_multipart_uploads, failed_uploads_5m, avg_upload_latency_ms_95, resume_success_rate, binder_validation_failures.
- Alerts: spike in failed_uploads or resume failures -> P0; spool disk > 80% -> P1 with automatic throttling.
- Runbook steps for common failures: resume upload, rebind bucket, rotate credentials, fallback to manual handoff.

Testing plan: 
- Unit: adapter auth flows, manifest generation, checksum verification.
- Integration: S3/GCS multipart/resume end-to-end with mocked network interruptions at part boundaries.
- On-prem: test against MinIO and Ceph with PUT-only backends and object compose tests.
- Compliance: simulated object-lock + legal hold scenarios to verify we can set flags when supported.

Rollout plan: 
1) Feature-flagged internal pilot in Redwood staging with a handful of internal tenants.
2) Invite-only private customers with small traffic to validate policies.
3) Incrementally increase buffered throughput and enable write-through after 2 weeks of no critical failures.
4) GA and documentation (hardening, operator guide, legal/SME signoffs).

Dependencies: ["ENG-62914", "ENG-33198", "ENG-41205", "ENG-48402"].

Open design questions: 
- Should we default to buffered mode for private installs to decouple ingestion SLAs from customer storage? Trade-off: buffered reduces tail-latency risk but requires local capacity management.
- Envelope key management: prefer pattern where Redwood never stores plaintext keys for envelope encryption; implement a per-tenant envelope key encrypted by customer KMS. Need legal confirmation for storing envelope ciphertext.
- How to represent manifests and receipts so that customers with restrictive bucket policies accept them (x-amz-meta vs separate manifest object).

Deliverables for this ticket: design doc in Confluence, proto implementation of adapter interface + S3/GCS adapters, local spool manager, manifest format spec, a small admin-console binding flow (UI stub), and an automated integration test suite.
